source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XI (Montreuil)

2.title: Elucidatio capituli secundi: Et iterum intravit Capharnaum post dies octo
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: “And again he entered into Capharnaum after eight days”

paras.t: Et iterum intravit Jesus Capharnaum post dies octo; [et auditum est quod in domo esset;] et convenerunt multi, ita ut non caperet, hoc est, contineri et capi seu stare non possent, neque ad januam domus in qua exstitit Christus. Sed aliqui ipsam domum introierunt. Et loquebatur eis verbum vitæ æternæ.
paras.en: [[2:1|And again he entered into Capharnaum|Et iterum intravit Jesus Capharnaum]] after eight days [Denis's text reads post dies octo, “after eight days”; the Vulgate has post dies, “after some days”]; [[2:2|and it was heard that he was in the house|et auditum est quod in domo esset]] [these words are supplied by the editors in brackets]; [[2:2|And many came together, so that there was no room|et convenerunt multi, ita ut non caperet]], that is, they could not be contained and held or find standing room, [[2:2|no, not even at the door|neque ad januam]] of the house in which Christ was. But some went into the house itself. [[2:2|And he spoke to them the word|Et loquebatur eis verbum]] of eternal life.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur curatio paralytici. De qua plenius dictum est in evangelio S. Matthæi: idcirco nunc celerius pertransibo. Et venerunt viri aliqui ferentes ad eum, hoc est ad Jesum, paralyticum, qui a quatuor portabatur una cum lecto in quo jacuit. Et quum non possent offerre, id est præsentare eum paralyticum illi, scilicet Christo, præ turba: quoniam propter turbam non poterant per januam ingredi domum in qua docuit Christus; nudaverunt tectum ubi erat, id est, tectum domus illius ascenderunt, et, facta illic apertura, per tegulas deposuerunt lectum cum languido. Unde nunc subditur: et patefacientes, id est, tectum illud aperientes, submiserunt grabatum in quo paralyticus jacebat. Tecta enim in locis illis plana fuerunt, habueruntque januam qua ad ea ascendebatur: per quam aliqui dicunt lectum fuisse submissum cum paralytico isto. Quia tamen hic dicitur quod nudaverunt tectum, et Lucas quoque ait quod per tegulas submiserunt infirmum, magis apparet quod in ipso tecto novam fecerunt aperturam.
paras.en: Next is described the healing of the paralytic, of which more has been said in the Gospel of St Matthew[[Matt 9:2||]] [the margin as read gives Matth. x, 2-7; the healing of the paralytic is Matt 9:2-7]; therefore I shall now pass over it more quickly. [[2:3|And they came|Et venerunt]], some men, [[2:3|to him, bringing|ferentes ad eum]], that is, to Jesus, [[2:3|one sick of the palsy, who was carried by four|paralyticum, qui a quatuor portabatur]], together with the bed on which he lay. [[2:4|And when they could not offer him|Et quum non possent offerre]], that is, present the paralytic to him, namely to Christ, [[2:4|for the multitude|præ turba]], since because of the crowd they could not enter by the door the house in which Christ was teaching, [[2:4|they uncovered the roof where he was|nudaverunt tectum ubi erat]], that is, they climbed onto the roof of that house and, making an opening there, let the bed down with the sick man through the tiles. So it is now added: [[2:4|and opening it|et patefacientes]], that is, opening that roof, [[2:4|they let down the bed wherein the man sick of the palsy lay|submiserunt grabatum in quo paralyticus jacebat]]. For the roofs in those parts were flat, and had a door by which one went up to them; and some say that the bed was let down with this paralytic through that door. But since it is said here that they uncovered the roof, and Luke too says that they let the sick man down [[Luke 5:19|through the tiles|per tegulas]], it seems more likely that they made a new opening in the roof itself.

paras.t: Cetera quæ hic de isto miraculo recitantur, patent ex his quæ in Matthæo dicta sunt. Hic tamen dicitur, quod Jesus cognovit spiritu suo cogitationes Scribarum. Et potest per spiritum Christi intelligi Spiritus Sanctus, de quo ait Apostolus: Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est ejus. Cujus utique Spiritus virtute et gratia, Christus ut homo agnovit cogitationes universorum. Et potest quoque per spiritum Christi intelligi intellectus animæ ejus, quo omnia præterita, præsentia et futura cognoscit.
paras.en: The rest of what is related here of this miracle is plain from what was said on Matthew. Here, however, it is said that Jesus knew [[2:8|in his spirit|spiritu suo]] the thoughts of the Scribes. And by the spirit of Christ may be understood the Holy Ghost, of whom the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:9|if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his|Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est ejus]]. By the power and grace of this Spirit, Christ as man knew the thoughts of all. And by the spirit of Christ may also be understood the intellect of His soul, by which He knows all things past, present and to come.

paras.t: Et egressus est rursus ad mare quod currit per Galilæam. Judæi autem quamlibet magnam congregationem aquarum nominant mare: quem loquendi modum servaverunt Evangelistæ. Et quum præteriret loca illa, vidit Levi Alphæi, id est Matthæum filium Alphæi: Matthæus enim alio nomine dictus est Levi; sedentem ad telonium. Porro, quæ subjunguntur hoc loco de vocatione Matthæi et punctis annexis, dicta atque exposita sunt in Matthæo.
paras.en: [[2:13|And he went forth again to the sea side|Et egressus est rursus ad mare]], the sea that runs through Galilee. For the Jews call any large gathering of waters a sea, and the Evangelists kept this manner of speaking. [[2:14|And when he was passing by|Et quum præteriret]] those parts, [[2:14|he saw Levi, the son of Alpheus|vidit Levi Alphæi]], that is, Matthew the son of Alpheus, for Matthew was also called by another name, Levi, [[2:14|sitting at the receipt of custom|sedentem ad telonium]]. What is added here about the calling of Matthew and the points connected with it has been said and explained on Matthew[[Matt 9:9||]] [the margin as read gives Matth. x, 9-13; the calling of Matthew is Matt 9:9-13].

paras.t: Deinceps Marcus describit disceptationem discipulorum Joannis et Pharisæorum cum Jesu; et littera patet plenissime ex his quæ in Matthæo dicta sunt.
paras.en: Next Mark describes the dispute of the disciples of John and of the Pharisees with Jesus; and the letter is entirely plain from what was said on Matthew[[Matt 9:14||]].

paras.t: Et factum est iterum quum sabbatis ambularet Jesus per sata. Hic Evangelista commemorat quomodo Jesu ambulante per agros seminatos et blada portantes, discipuli ejus fame compulsi, spicas sumpserunt et comederunt: quo viso Pharisæi increpabant Christum. Quidquid autem hic scribitur de hoc facto, supra expositum est in Matthæo. Sed quærendum est, quomodo Marcus dicat ipsum David intrasse domum Dei sub Abiathar principe sacerdotum, quum in libris Regum legatur id factum sub Achimelech pontifice? Et respondendum, quod iste Abiathar fuit filius Achimelech, succedens ei in sacerdotii principatu; et patre ejus vivente, egit interdum vices ipsius: ideo David dicitur introisse domum Dei sub eo.
paras.en: [[2:23|And it came to pass again, as the Lord walked through the corn fields on the sabbath|Et factum est iterum quum sabbatis ambularet Jesus per sata]]. Here the Evangelist records how, as Jesus walked through fields that were sown and bearing grain, His disciples, driven by hunger, took ears of corn and ate them; seeing which, the Pharisees rebuked Christ. Whatever is written here of this deed has been explained above on Matthew[[Matt 12:1||]]. But it must be asked how Mark can say that David himself [[2:26|went into the house of God, under Abiathar the high priest|intrasse domum Dei sub Abiathar principe sacerdotum]], when in the books of Kings we read that it was done under the high priest Achimelech[[1 Kings 21:1||]]. And the answer is that this Abiathar was the son of Achimelech, who succeeded him in the chief priesthood; and while his father was still living he sometimes acted in his place: so David is said to have entered the house of God under him.

3.title: Expositio capituli tertii: Et introivit iterum in synagogam
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: “And he entered again into the synagogue”

paras.t: Deinde recitat Evangelista quomodo Christus sanaverit hominem cujus aruit manus. Et planus est sensus hujus loci ex his quæ in Matthæo dicta sunt. Et circumspiciens Jesus eos, id est incredulos Judæos ac Pharisæos, cum ira per zelum, id est cum moderato appetitu vindictæ propter injuriam Deo illatam, vel saltem cum vultu iram prætendente. Fuit autem in Christo ira per zelum: quæ tamen actum rationis in ipso nullatenus perturbabat, quia in ipso unaquæque potentia animæ exercuit actum suum, non impediendo alterius actum potentiæ. In aliis tamen ira, etiam quæ est per zelum, turbat aliqualiter oculum mentis, quoniam anima circa actum unius potentiæ multum intenta et occupata, impeditur in actu alterius potentiæ. Hæc autem ira mansuetudini non repugnat, cujus est passionem iræ ordinare; sed ira per vitium. Contristatus super cæcitate cordis eorum, misericorditer condolens eis. Fuit ergo in Christo tristitia virtuosa ex caritate et pietate descendens, quia errantibus compatiebatur. Fuit quoque in eo passio tristitiæ moderata ac naturalis, quia inferior pars animæ ejus sequebatur partem superiorem. Quod autem in Isaia de Christo inducitur, Non erit tristis nec turbulentus, intelligendum est de sæculari, carnali et inordinata tristitia, quæ non cadit in virum perfectum, quemadmodum Salomon contestatur: Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit.
paras.en: Next the Evangelist relates how Christ healed the man whose hand was withered; and the sense of this passage is plain from what was said on Matthew[[Matt 12:10||]] [the margin prints Matth. xi, 10-13; the healing of the withered hand is Matt 12:10-13]. [[3:5|And looking round about on them|Et circumspiciens eos]], that is, on the unbelieving Jews and Pharisees, [[3:5|with anger|cum ira]], an anger of zeal, that is, with a measured desire to punish the injury done to God, or at least with a countenance that showed anger. There was in Christ the anger of zeal [ira per zelum: anger roused by zeal for what is right, as distinct from ira per vitium, the sinful anger of vice], which nevertheless in no way disturbed the act of reason in Him, because in Him each power of the soul exercised its own act without hindering the act of another power. In others, however, anger, even the anger of zeal, somewhat clouds the eye of the mind, because the soul, much intent upon and occupied with the act of one power, is hindered in the act of another. This anger is not opposed to meekness, whose part is to order the passion of anger; what is opposed to it is the anger of vice. [[3:5|being grieved for the blindness of their hearts|contristatus super cæcitate cordis eorum]], mercifully grieving with them. So there was in Christ a virtuous sadness coming down from charity and pity, because He felt compassion for those who went astray. There was in Him also a moderate and natural passion of sadness, because the lower part of His soul followed the higher. And what is brought forward in Isaias concerning Christ, [[Is 42:4|He shall not be sad, nor troublesome|Non erit tristis, neque turbulentus]], is to be understood of worldly, carnal and disordered sadness, which does not befall a perfect man, as Solomon testifies: [[Prov 12:21|Whatsoever shall befall the just man, shall not make him sad|Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit]].

paras.t: Exeuntes autem Pharisæi, cum Herodianis, id est militibus Herodis, vel, ut alii dicunt, cum his qui putabant Herodem esse Christum, consilium faciebant quomodo illum perderent, id est, qualiter Jesum occiderent.
paras.en: [[3:6|And the Pharisees going out|Exeuntes autem pharisæi]] [[3:6|made a consultation with the Herodians|cum Herodianis consilium faciebant]], that is, with Herod's soldiers, or, as others say, with those who thought that Herod was the Christ, [[3:6|how they might destroy him|quomodo eum perderent]], that is, how they might kill Jesus.

paras.t: Et Jesus cum discipulis suis secessit ad mare, dans locum furentibus. Et dixit discipulis suis ut navicula sibi deserviret, id est, navem sibi adducerent, eamque intraret, et staret in mari juxta ripam, propter turbam stantem et accurrentem in terra, ne comprimerent eum. In quo ostendit se vere fuisse passibilem, atque sæpe ad tempus vitasse incommoda corporis, ut tempore divinitus præstituto pateretur. Et quamvis poterat turbæ pressuram sine læsione et pœna sustinere per viam mirabilem, noluit tamen humanum subsidium devitare, ut veritatem assumptæ naturæ ostenderet. Multos enim sanabat, ita ut irruerent in eum ut illum tangerent. Nam virtus exibat de illo, sanabatque omnes.
paras.en: [[3:7|But Jesus retired with his disciples to the sea|Jesus autem cum discipulis suis secessit ad mare]], giving way to their fury. [[3:9|And he spoke to his disciples that a small ship should wait on him|Et dicit discipulis suis ut navicula sibi deserviret]]: that is, that they should bring a boat to Him, so that He might go into it and stand on the water near the shore, [[3:9|because of the multitude|propter turbam]] standing and running together on the land, [[3:9|lest they should throng him|ne comprimerent eum]]. In this He showed that He was truly able to suffer, and that He often avoided bodily hardships for a time, so that He might suffer at the time divinely appointed. And though He could have borne the pressing of the crowd without hurt or pain by a miraculous way, He would not refuse a human help, so as to show the reality of the nature He had taken. [[3:10|For he healed many, so that they pressed upon him for to touch him|multos enim sanabat, ita ut irruerent in eum ut illum tangerent]]. For [[Luke 6:19|virtue went out from him and healed all|virtus de illo exibat, et sanabat omnes]].

paras.t: Quotquot autem habebant plagas, id est varias infirmitates, et spiritus immundi, id est diaboli in obsessis; vel, Spiritus immundi, id est obsessi a dæmonibus; quum illum videbant, procidebant ei, sponte vel coacte reverentiam exhibendo: et si aliqui languidi talem infirmitatem habebant, quod ante suam curationem se coram Jesu prosternere non valebant, tamen sanitate recepta, hoc facere poterant. Et clamabant dæmones per obsessos, dicentes: Tu es Filius Dei. Hoc conjecturaliter asserebant, non cum certitudine constanti et absoluta. Et vehementer comminabatur eis ne manifestarent illum, id est, ne ultra dicerent coram populo Jesum esse Christum Filium Dei. Contempsit enim testimonium dæmonum, propter causas introductas. Sed cur dæmones dixerunt tot bona de Christo? Dicendum, quod coacte vel malo fine, et ob alias causas quas non est facile excogitare: et forte, ut ejus passionem impedirent, scientes quod nunquam crucifigerent Dominum gloriæ ipsi Judæi, si eum agnoscerent.
paras.en: [[3:10|as many as had evils|quotquot habebant plagas]], that is, various sicknesses, [[3:11|And the unclean spirits|Et spiritus immundi]], that is, the devils in the possessed; or, 'the unclean spirits', that is, those possessed by demons, [[3:11|when they saw him, fell down before him|cum illum videbant, procidebant ei]], showing reverence willingly or under compulsion. And if some of the sick had such an infirmity that they could not prostrate themselves before Jesus before they were cured, yet once their health was restored they could do so. [[3:11|and they cried, saying|et clamabant, dicentes]], the demons speaking through the possessed: [[3:12|Thou art the Son of God.|Tu es Filius Dei.]] This they asserted by conjecture, not with constant and absolute certainty. [[3:12|And he strictly charged them that they should not make him known.|Et vehementer comminabatur eis ne manifestarent illum.]] That is, that they should no longer say before the people that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of God; for He scorned the testimony of demons, for the reasons given earlier[[Mark 1:25||]]. But why did the demons say so many good things of Christ? It must be said: under compulsion, or with an evil purpose, and for other reasons not easy to work out; and perhaps to hinder His passion, knowing that the Jews themselves would never crucify the Lord of glory if they recognized Him[[1 Cor 2:8||]].

paras.t: Et ascendens Jesus in montem, vocavit ad se quos voluit ipse, id est quos præ aliis ad hoc elegit, videlicet quosdam ex discipulis; et venerunt ad eum in montem. Et fecit ut essent duodecim cum illo, id est, duodecim Apostolos fecit sibi specialiter adhærere, ut essent sibi quasi collaterales, familiares et proximi; et ut mitteret eos prædicare. Et imposuit Simoni nomen aliud, scilicet Petrus, quod interpretatur firmus, sive obediens principalis. Et Jacobum filium Zebedæi, et Joannem fratrem Jacobi vocavit, et imposuit eis nomina Boanerges, quod est, filii tonitrui, propter altisonam et efficacissimam prædicationem ipsorum, et quia in transfiguratione Christi audierunt, vel potius audituri erant vocem Patris dicentis: Hic est Filius meus dilectus. Hujuscemodi enim vox appellatur tonitruum, eo modo quo scriptum est in Job: Quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis ejus intueri? Hæc autem mutatio nominum spiritualem innovationem et gratiam specialem designavit. Cetera quæ hic dicuntur, plenius elucidata sunt in Matthæo.
paras.en: [[3:13|And going up into a mountain, he called unto him whom he would himself|Et ascendens in montem vocavit ad se quos voluit ipse]], that is, those whom He chose for this before others, namely some of the disciples; [[3:13|and they came to him|et venerunt ad eum]] on the mountain. [[3:14|And he made that twelve should be with him|Et fecit ut essent duodecim cum illo]]: that is, He made twelve Apostles cleave to Him in a special way, to be, as it were, His companions at His side, His familiars and His nearest; [[3:14|and that he might send them to preach|et ut mitteret eos prædicare]]. [[3:16|And to Simon he gave the name|Et imposuit Simoni nomen]], a new one, namely Peter, which is interpreted 'firm', or 'obedient chief'. And He called [[3:17|James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he named them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder|Jacobum Zebedæi, et Joannem fratrem Jacobi, et imposuit eis nomina Boanerges, quod est, Filii tonitrui]], because of their lofty-sounding and most effective preaching, and because at Christ's transfiguration they heard, or rather were to hear, the voice of the Father saying: [[Matt 17:5|This is my beloved Son|Hic est Filius meus dilectus]]. For such a voice is called thunder, in the way it is written in Job: [[Job 26:14|who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness|quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis illius intueri]]? This change of names signified a spiritual renewal and a special grace. The rest of what is said here was more fully explained on Matthew[[Matt 10:1||]].

paras.t: Et veniunt ad domum. Et convenit iterum turba ad Jesum, ut salutis verbum audirent, ita ut non possent neque panem manducare, id est, tam ferventer ac perseveranter insistebat Christus verbo prædicationis, quod discipuli ejus non habebant quietum tempus ad manducandum. Et quum audissent sui, id est, quum discipuli Christi: et maxime quidam ex consanguineis suis ex parte Matris, de quibus ait Joannes, quod fratres ejus nondum credebant in eum: quum igitur isti audissent verba Jesu, quæ erant supernaturalia, ardua, insolita, rudibusque Judæis penitus inaudita, exierunt tenere eum, hoc est comprehendere vel ligare Jesum tanquam arrepticium vel insanum. Dicebant enim: Quoniam in furorem versus est, id est furiosus effectus. Quoniam enim audierunt eum talia prædicare, nec a prædicatione cessare, nec corporalia commoda curare, opinati sunt quod esset in furorem conversus: quemadmodum Festus ait ad Paulum, Multæ litteræ ad insaniam te convertunt. Voluerunt ergo Jesum tenere, ne ex insania, sibi ipsi vel aliis nocumentum inferret. Et Scribæ qui ab Jerosolymis descenderant, dicebant: Quoniam Beelzebub habet, id est, dæmone sic vocato obsessus est, et quia in principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia. Locus iste in Matthæo plene atque diffuse expositus est, ita ut illis pensatis, ista facillime intelligantur. Item quod subditur, Et veniunt Mater ejus et fratres, explanatum quoque est in Matthæo.
paras.en: [[3:20|And they come to a house, and the multitude cometh together again|Et veniunt ad domum: et convenit iterum turba]] to Jesus, to hear the word of salvation, [[3:20|so that they could not so much as eat bread|ita ut non possent neque panem manducare]]: that is, Christ kept at the word of preaching so fervently and so constantly that His disciples had no quiet time to eat. [[3:21|And when his friends had heard of it|Et cum audissent sui]]: that is, Christ's disciples, and especially certain of His kinsmen on His Mother's side, of whom John says that [[John 7:5|neither did his brethren believe in him|neque enim fratres ejus credebant in eum]]; when these, then, had heard the words of Jesus, which were supernatural, lofty, unaccustomed and wholly unheard-of to the unlettered Jews, [[3:21|they went out to lay hold on him|exierunt tenere eum]], that is, to seize or bind Jesus as one possessed or insane. [[3:21|For they said: He is become mad.|dicebant enim: Quoniam in furorem versus est.]] That is, He has become raving. For since they heard Him preaching such things, never ceasing from preaching, and taking no care for bodily comforts, they supposed He had turned to madness, as Festus said to Paul: [[Acts 26:24|much learning doth make thee mad|multæ te litteræ ad insaniam convertunt]]. So they wanted to hold Jesus, lest in His madness He should do harm to Himself or to others. [[3:22|And the scribes who were come down from Jerusalem, said: He hath Beelzebub|Et scribæ, qui ab Jerosolymis descenderant, dicebant: Quoniam Beelzebub habet]], that is, He is possessed by the demon so called, [[3:22|and by the prince of devils he casteth out devils|et quia in principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]. This passage was expounded fully and at length on Matthew[[Matt 12:24||]], so that once that is weighed, this is very easily understood. Likewise what follows, [[3:31|And his mother and his brethren came|Et veniunt mater ejus et fratres]], was also explained on Matthew[[Matt 12:46||]].
